document_candidates.title: 1995 ANKARA 008128 DEMIREL CAUTIONS AGAINST "MUSLIM FORCE" IN BOSNIA WHILE PUBLIC ANGER HEATS UP
document_candidates.repository: Department of State, FOIA Virtual Reading Room
document_candidates.action: Embassy Ankara reports Turkish public anger after Srebrenica and Demirel's rejection of a separate Muslim force if UNPROFOR withdraws. Use this reported position or contact to test how US diplomacy reconciled allied, regional and institutional constraints during the Bosnia crisis. document_candidates.title: 1995 BELGRADE 003330 BOSNIA AIRSTRIKES: BELGRADE EAC MEETING

chronology.label: 1995 ANKARA 008128 DEMIREL CAUTIONS AGAINST "MUSLIM FORCE" IN BOSNIA WHILE PUBLIC ANGER HEATS UP
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Ankara reports Turkish public anger after Srebrenica and Demirel's rejection of a separate Muslim force if UNPROFOR withdraws.

chronology.label: 1995 ATHENS 006392 GREECE SEEKING NEW PEACE CONFERENCE FOR BOSNIA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Athens reports Papoulias's proposed peace conference and sanctions relief, while cautioning that the proposal lacked developed staff work.

chronology.label: 1995 ATHENS 006432 RECRUITING GREEK VOLUNTEERS FOR BOSNIA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Athens reports press claims about Greek volunteers in Bosnia and a Croatian complaint; these are reported allegations, not verified participation findings.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003330 BOSNIA AIRSTRIKES: BELGRADE EAC MEETING
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Belgrade's Emergency Action Committee adopted a modified standfast after NATO airstrikes; no threats had been reported at the stated time.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003374 DEMARCHE TO MILOSEVIC ON SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Perina reports delivering a demarche to Milosevic, who denied responsibility for Srebrenica and claimed limited contact with Mladic. Those claims require corroboration.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003378 MODIFIED STANDFAST LIFTED
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Belgrade planned to lift modified standfast after reviewing local reaction and security, while preserving readiness for a renewed threat.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003433 DUTCH PEACEKEEPERS RELEASED FROM SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Bildt reported the expected transfer of Dutch hostages, with the number explicitly still being verified; a separate telegram was to explain the negotiations.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003434 NEGOTIATING WITH MILOSEVIC AND EACH OTHER: BILDT, STOLTENBERG AND AKASHI MEETING
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Record of the July 15 meeting of Bildt, Stoltenberg, Akashi, Rupert Smith and diplomatic representatives on negotiations with Milosevic and the Bosnia peace process.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003435 MESSAGE FROM ICFY NEGOTIATOR CARL BILDT
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Telegram transmits Bildt's message on Belgrade talks and anticipated practical results; anticipated measures must be distinguished from completed implementation.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003460 ICRC/BELGRADE DOES NOT SEE ACCESS - TO BRATUNAC DETAINEES COMING SOON
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. ICRC's acting director reported continuing denial of access to Bratunac detainees while medical evacuations occupied the agency.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003588 BELGRADE WARNS BOSNIAN SERBS NOT TO ATTACK - GORAZDE; REACTION TO LONDON CONFERENCE MUTED
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Belgrade reports an official warning against attacking Gorazde and muted reactions to the London conference, including emphasis on Russian positions.

chronology.label: 1995 BELGRADE 003708 CODEL HALL TELLS PALE LEADERSHIP IT SHOULD - IMPROVE HUMANITARIAN ACCESS
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. CODEL Hall's meetings provide a congressional channel for humanitarian-access representations; the telegram also records FRY claims on Kosovo, sanctions and Yugoslav dissolution.

chronology.label: 1995 BONN 013851 BOSNIA - STOLTENBERG WARNS OF UNPROFOR WITHDRAWAL IN TALK WITH GERMAN FOREIGN MINISTER
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A German diplomatic account records Kinkel's skepticism toward Milosevic and Bildt's negotiations and Stoltenberg's concerns about Croatian military action.

chronology.label: 1995 BONN 013852 BOSNIA - GERMANY CONCERNED ABOUT SREBRENICA AND EFFECT ON RAPID REACTION FORCE AND UNPROFOR
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. German officials linked the Srebrenica crisis to possible Croatian action, falling support for UNPROFOR and risks to the Rapid Reaction Force.

chronology.label: 1995 BONN 013928 FRANCO-GERMAN SUMMIT: BOSNIA OVERSHADOWS OTHER ISSUES, SATELLITES DISCUSSED ONLY WITH PRESS
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Bonn reports that Bosnia dominated the July 11 Franco-German summit; its assessment distinguishes Kohl's public support from reservations about Chirac's approach.

chronology.label: 1995 BONN 014037 GERMAN HIGH-LEVEL STRATEGY SESSION ON BOSNIA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A German account of the July 13 strategy meeting describes Kohl's advice to Chirac and the conditions Germany placed on military action after Srebrenica.

chronology.label: 1995 BONN 014157 GERMAN TORNADO DEPLOYMENT PROCEEDS WITHOUT CONTROVERSY IN THE WAKE OF SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Bonn reports continued deployment preparations for German support to the Rapid Reaction Force, subject to the limited parliamentary mandate.

chronology.label: 1995 BONN 014269 BOSNIA - GERMAN FOREIGN MINISTER REACTS NEGATIVELY TO BILDT EU BRIEFING
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. German officials criticized Bildt's interest in further sanctions concessions and questioned the political acceptability of dealings with Mladic after Srebrenica.

chronology.label: 1995 BRUSSELS 007182 BELGIAN GOVERNMENT APPROVES PARATROOPER CONTINGENT FOR RAPID REACTION FORCE; APPROVES USE OF 'MOVING STAR' TRANSPORT UNIT FOR SARAJEVO
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Telegram reports Belgian troop and transport commitments to the Rapid Reaction Force, drawing in part on public government and press accounts.

chronology.label: 1995 COPENHAGEN 003843 FROM LEOPARD TANKS TO REFUGEE TENTS: LOCAL COLOR ON DANISH PEACEKEEPING IN BOSNIA

chronology.label: 1995 DOHA 001609 QATAR AND BOSNIA: GROWING AWARENESS, GROWING TENSION
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Doha reports Qatari media reactions to Srebrenica, Zepa, the London conference and the American arms-embargo debate.

chronology.label: 1995 DUBLIN 003631 IRELAND AND BOSNIA: KEEPING A LOW PROFILE

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005347 BOSNIA: UNHCR PESSIMISTIC ON PRESENT SITUATION - AND ABILITY TO OPERATE DURING AN UNPROFOR WITHDRAWAL

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005445 SREBRENICA: GOBH OPPOSING EVACUATION; UNHCR - NEEDS ACCESS, NOT SUPPLIES

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005475 SREBRENICA: UNHCR AND ICRC ACTIVITIES

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005518 TUZLA: BOSNIAN AUTHORITIES AGREE TO - PROVIDE COLLECTION CENTERS FOR DISPLACED

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005633 ICRC CAUTIONS ON POSSIBLE INTERNATIONALLY- SUPERVISED EVACUATION PLAN FOR GORAZDE, CONCERNED ABOUT SERIOUS FUNDING SHORTFALLS AFFECTING OPERATIONS
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. ICRC discussion with Oakley and Spiegel addresses detainee access, medical evacuations and cautions about internationally supervised evacuations.

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005670 PLANS FOR ZEPA EVACUATION
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. UNHCR and ICRC lacked permission to participate in the Zepa evacuation; the telegram records Mladic's stated plans for separating males and permitting access.

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005715 BOSNIA UPDATE, 21 JULY
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Humanitarian update reports convoy arrivals, displaced-person estimates and Dutchbat departure. Figures within the extracted text need reconciliation against the PDF.

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005826 ZEPA EVACUATION: REGISTRATION IN ENCLAVES
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Geneva reports prospective Zepa evacuation arrangements, access claims and humanitarian agencies' objections to registering people in other enclaves.

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005829 ZEPA EVACUATION: REGISTRATION IN ENCLAVES
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A separately numbered Geneva cable reports similar Zepa evacuation and registration concerns. Compare it with Geneva 5826 rather than collapsing the copies.

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005948 SHATTUCK MISSION TO BOSNIA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Shattuck reports conclusions and urgent recommendations after visiting Bosnia; the text explicitly points to a forthcoming detailed report and refugee accounts.

chronology.label: 1995 GENEVA 005949 URGENT ACTION REQUIRED ON BOSNIA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. After Shattuck's mission, Geneva flags two urgent issues for Washington's review alongside Bildt's visit and forthcoming Geneva meetings.

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 010050 BOSNIA: VIEWS OF FCO MINISTER OF STATE

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 010113 BRITISH CABINET DECISIONS ON BOSNIA

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 010114 BRITISH CHOD ON BOSNIA

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 009740 JOHN MAJOR'S VIEWS POST-SREBRENICA

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 009772 BRITISH FOREIGN SECRETARY ON SREBRENICA

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 009839 DUTCH CONCERNS RE PRESS IMAGE ON SREBRENICA

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 009894 BOSNIA: MAJOR AND CHIRAC TO DISCUSS DIFFERENCES AND NEXT STEPS

chronology.label: 1995 LONDON 009935 JULY 13 RIFKIND-SACIRBEY MEETING

chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Bosnia’s charge rejected the possible deployment of Russian peacekeepers to Gorazde as unacceptable, giving a Bosnian perspective on Russian participation.

chronology.label: 1995 WARSAW 010273 MAZOWIECKI CALLS FOR UNITY IN CONFRONTING BOSNIAN SERBS; REQUESTS TIMETABLE FOR QUICKER NATO EXPANSION
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A shortened Warsaw copy reports Mazowiecki’s call for Western unity and faster NATO expansion but jumps over numbered paragraphs; compare the fuller Warsaw 10279 copy.

chronology.label: 1995 WARSAW 010279  MAZOWIECKI CALLS FOR UNITY IN CONFRONTING BOSNIAN SERBS; REQUESTS TIMETABLE FOR QUICKER NATO EXPANSION
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. The fuller Warsaw account connects Mazowiecki’s human-rights mission and criticism of negotiations without credible Western action with his views on NATO enlargement.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002566 SERB ATTACK ON SREBRENICA EVOKES A UN "WARNING"
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Zagreb reports the UN warning to Mladic and distinguishes a warning from an ultimatum; it documents command judgments before Srebrenica fell.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002570  AKASHI AND JANVIER DEFEND ACTIONS ON SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Akashi and Janvier explained their warnings and communications with Bosnian Serb commanders during the July 10 embassy approach.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002590  UNPROFOR CONSIDERING NEXT STEPS IN LIGHT OF SERB ULTIMATUM ON SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. UN contacts treated reported Serb evacuation demands seriously while sources and reassurance from Tolimir remained conflicting.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002592 UNPROFOR MOVES FROM DEFENDING SREBRENICA TO DEFENDING ITS REFUGEES; ZEPA MAY BE NEXT
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Zagreb records UNPROFOR’s shift to protecting people at Potocari and the uncertainty surrounding extraction reports.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002601  SREBRENICA: MLADIC THREATENS TO SHELL POTOCARI; DUTCHBAT DESPAIRING OF ITS MISSION
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Zagreb describes Mladic’s demands, Dutchbat’s difficulty protecting civilians and troops and reported threats around Potocari.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002608 UPDATE ON SITUATION IN SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A UN adviser described Bosnian opposition to emptying the enclave and UNHCR’s obligation to respect individual requests to depart.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002615 SREBRENICA UPDATE: BSA TAKES AWAY DRAFT AGE MALES; UNPROFOR SPOKESMAN CRITICIZES THE UNSC
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. UN reporting records separation of military-age men, uncertain detention locations, food shortages and refugee movements toward Tuzla.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002622 GRANIC SAYS CROATIA WILL NOT REACT TO SREBRENICA WANTS PRESSURE ON BELGRADE, LAYS DOWN MARKERS ON UNCRO, BIHAC
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Granic blamed Belgrade and promised restraint while warning that threats to Bihac could widen the war and challenging UNCRO’s performance.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002623 BOSNIAN AMBASSADOR TRNKA ON SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Bosnian Ambassador Trnka described mistreatment of refugees and requests for Ogata’s intervention, medical assistance and monitoring.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002627 SREBRENLCA: THE PROBLEMS MULTIPLY
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A UN adviser reported refugee-processing figures, separation of military-age men and difficulties with shelter, water and relief delivery.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002629 SREBRENICA: MOST REFUGEES OUT OF POTOCARI: ATROCITIES REPORTED: CONSPIRACY THEORIES ABOUND
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Zagreb reports refugee movements and detention estimates and emerging atrocity reports; these contemporaneous estimates and theories require corroboration.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002647 ZEPA ENCLAVE UNDER ATTACK, RIPE TO FALL
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Zagreb describes attacks on Zepa and conflicting or unconfirmed reports about Ukrainian troops and Serb warnings.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002648 SREBRENICA UPDATE: REFUGEE MOVEMENT, STRANDED MEDEVACS, LACK OF COOPERATION ON EVERY SIDE
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A donor briefing and UN contacts describe relief bottlenecks and deaths among stranded medical evacuees; UNHCR could not then confirm atrocity reports.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002659 UN UPDATE ON BOSNIAN SITUATION
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. UN reporting describes the deteriorating military position around Zepa and an expectation of its fall; the prediction is not the date of actual capture.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002663 JANVIER RECOMMENDS A MORE ROBUST MILITARY RESPONSE
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Janvier’s July 17 memorandum recommended a more robust response at Gorazde and considered the risk that strikes on integrated air defenses could be seen as war.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002710 KRAJINA SERBS LAUNCH ASSAULT ON BIHAC
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. UNPF sources described Krajina Serb attacks and shelling around Bihac, providing field reporting for the risk of Croatian intervention.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002748 AKASHI SAYS UN FORCES HAVE NOT TAKEN PRECAUTIONS AGAINST HOSTAGE TAKING, PROMISES TO "GET UNDERWAY"
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Galbraith pressed Akashi on hostage prevention; Akashi acknowledged that planning had begun but had not been implemented.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002784 UN OFFICIALS SAY "ARSK" ATTACK ON BIHAC LIMITED, EXPECT GOC REACTION BEFORE NOVEMBER
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A UN commander assessed the Bihac operation as limited and discussed possible Croatian action; retain the assessment’s authorship rather than treating it as settled fact.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002788 POSSIBLE MASS EXECUTION OF SREBRENICA MALES IS REASON TO SAVE ZEPA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Embassy Zagreb urged reconsidering airstrikes for Zepa in light of a survivor account and reports of a possible Srebrenica massacre.

chronology.label: 1995 ZAGREB 002883 CODEL KERREY
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. Congressional-visit arrangements include a Croatia security assessment. Administrative details have limited selection value but can anchor travel and briefing reconstruction.

chronology.label: 1995 USUN NEW YORK 002750 JULY 10: DRAFT RESOLUTION ON SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A distinct USUN New York copy records the Srebrenica draft-resolution discussion; retain the full URL to distinguish it from the USUNN and State copies.

chronology.label: 1995 USUN NEW YORK 002720 JULY 10: SC DISCUSSION OF SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A distinct USUN New York copy preserves the July 10 Security Council discussion; compare routing, completeness and excisions with the USUNN version.

chronology.label: 1995 USUN NEW YORK 002731 NO USE OF NATO CLOSE AIR SUPPORT NEAR -- SREBRENICA
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A distinct USUN New York copy preserves the correction that NATO close air support had not occurred on the earlier reported occasion.

chronology.label: 1995 USUN NEW YORK 002781 BOSNIA: SECRETARIAT ON SITUATION IN -- SREBRENICA, NEXT STEPS
chronology.note: Catalog/document transmission date; any earlier event described in the text is not silently substituted. A distinct USUN New York copy preserves the Secretariat account of forced evacuation, detained men and denied access; compare it with the USUNN version.

chronology.label: Security  Council RESOLUTION 1022 (1995)
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Resolution 1022, adopted November 22, 1995, suspends sanctions with conditions, links Bosnian Serb relief to withdrawal and provides mechanisms for reimposition.

chronology.label: Serbia's support to the Bosnian Serbs
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Forwarded assessment discusses continuing military supplies to Bosnian Serbs and limitations of border monitoring and interdiction.

chronology.label: Need for MKA response
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Jones relays MKA replies on improving credibility/timing of material, exploring ICTY information sharing and daily update calls.

chronology.label: Yugo/ExclZones
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Rashkow insists that use-of-force/exclusion-zone papers receive legal clearance and that NATO establishment of zones requires UN concurrence.

chronology.label: SERBS FLOUT U.N. WEAPON-FREE ZONES
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Reuters reports violations of Sarajevo/Gorazde weapons-exclusion zones and UN officers’ caution about retaliation against peacekeepers.

chronology.label: SERBS FLOUT BOSNIAN EXCLUSION ZONE AROUND GORAZDE
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Reuters describes July 25 Gorazde exclusion-zone violations and reported limits on effective enforcement.

chronology.label: SERBS FLOUT BOSNIAN EXCLUSION ZONE AROUND GORAZDE
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Second copy of the July 25 Reuters Gorazde exclusion-zone dispatch.

chronology.label: the cable
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Kimble warns that an instruction-like cable to Akashi should reflect MKA’s New York contact to avoid resistance and reinforce messages from his superiors.

chronology.label: Changes to the Military Annex to the Peace Plan
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Holbrooke and the U.S. delegation request Deputies review of Bosnian proposed military-annex changes, oppose mission creep and request guidance on other changes.

chronology.label: AGREEMENT ON THE MILITARY ASPECTS OF THE PEACE SETTLEMENT
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Bosnian delegation’s proposed changes to Annex 1 address military obligations and IFOR arrangements in a marked-up draft.

chronology.label: BOSNIA: NOVEMBER 13 DISCUSSION BY THE CONTACT GROUP PLUS ITALY OF RUSSIAN DRAFT LETTER TO THE SGY, RUSSIAN DRAFT RESOLUTIONS ON FRY SANCTIONS, AND NEXT STEPS ON EASTERN SLAVONIA
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. USUN reports November 13 Contact Group-plus-Italy discussions with Lavrov over Russian drafts on IFOR consultation, sanctions relief and Eastern Slavonia.

chronology.label: Bosnia Sanction Res
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Cover debates wording for sanctions termination, noncompliance, frozen funds and anticipated Russian objections while circulating an updated draft.

chronology.label: Bosnia Economic Sanctions Suspension UNSC Resolution
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. November 13 revision 4 proposes sanctions suspension in renewable 60 day periods and conditions governing relief, frozen assets and financing.

chronology.label: East Slavonia issues
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Hoh urges securing FRY-Croatia mutual recognition, resolving operation design and beginning consultations on Eastern Slavonia implementation.

chronology.label: GOC AND EASTERN SLAVONIAN SERBS SIGN AGREEMENT ON EASTERN SLAVONIA
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Zagreb reports signature of the Eastern Slavonia agreement and transmits its text on transitional administration, rights and peaceful reintegration.

chronology.label: Establishment of Executive Committee on Implementation of a Peace Settlement in Bosnia-Herzegovina
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Lake establishes a Bosnia Implementation Ex Comm, specifies co-chairs and reporting to Deputies/Principals, and asks agencies to designate senior representatives.

chronology.label: Bosnia Excomm
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Moon reports Ex Comm meeting arrangements, a separate war crimes chapter and a USUN/IO paper on civilian UN agencies.

chronology.label: ANNEX: LONDON CONFERENCE PREPARATION TIMELINE
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. November 8 draft lays out proposed London conference preparations and IFOR sequencing while discussing French/British/Russian preferences, congressional support and UNSC timing.

chronology.label: OGATA PLEADS WITH JOULWAN TO KEEP UNPROFOR CIVILIAN FUNCTIONS IN THE FORMER YUGOSLAVIA
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Geneva reports Ogata/Joulwan concerns that civilian functions and coordination remain unsettled as IFOR planning advances.

chronology.label: IFOR-UNHCR PLANNING FOR THE FORMER YUGOSLAVIA:    A GOOD FIT
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Geneva reports Joulwan/Ogata planning on logistics, security, information exchange, civilian coordination and exit strategies.

chronology.label: DC at 12:30 p.m. today
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Scheffer criticizes the NSC game plan, opposes a Greater Serbia/secession outcome, discusses sanctions leverage and proposes arming options within existing UN authorities.

chronology.label: Weekend discussions on Bosnia  Talking Points for Quad and CG Meetings on July 24
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Scheffer reviews weekend discussion of Dole-Lieberman, arms-embargo lift, dual key, Bildt plan and post-UNPROFOR options while proposing talking points.

chronology.label: NATO Planning for UN Withdrawal From Bosnia 'Complete'
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. AFP/FBIS report describes NATO withdrawal planning as technically complete but awaiting political approval.

chronology.label: REHABILITATION/RECONSTRUCTION  PROJECTS
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Paper estimates funding for employment, schools, power, health and infrastructure and lists potential Islamic donors.

chronology.label: ceasefire violations; serbs shoot at five un planes, causing two casualtiea; worst shelling and sniping since ceasefire
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Sarajevo reports firing on UN aircraft, airport closure and local reaction, alongside Mostar’s handover to EU administration.

chronology.label: FIFTH COMMITTEE ACTION: UNPROFOR. MINURSO, WAR CRIMES TRIBUNAL
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. USUN reports Fifth Committee financing decisions for UNPROFOR/MINURSO and the war crimes tribunal, with commentary on budget negotiation.

chronology.label: URGENT: attack on Dutch
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Chamberlin relays Dutch mission report of attack on Dutch forces near Srebrenica and UN confirmation that close air support was requested.

chronology.label: Bosnian Serbs say they allowed pilot rescue
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Reuters compares Bosnian Serb claims about allowing O’Grady rescue with NATO statements that rescuers came under fire.

chronology.label: Economic  and  Social Council SITUATION OF HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE TERRITORY OF THE FORMER YUGOSLAVIA
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Mazowiecki’s fifth periodic report surveys human rights violations across Bosnia, Croatia and FRY and presents conclusions/recommendations.

chronology.label: Talking  Points
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Talking points discuss Commission of Experts annexes, Goldstone’s public strategy, anticipated risks to enclaves and Tribunal resources.

chronology.label: Talking  Points
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Talking points discuss publication of Bassiouni annexes and criticize management/resources in ICTY prosecution while advocating U.S. assistance.

chronology.label: WAR CRIMES TRIBUNAL
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. March 28 draft describes Tribunal start-up, staffing and U.S. intention to consider cooperation in sanctions decisions.

chronology.label: Bosnia SVTS - 7/12
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. George’s July 12 notes record French positions, debate over the Contact Group plan and support for reestablishing Srebrenica while planning further strategy.

chronology.label: bosnia svits 6/22 et. al.
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Notes report June 21 presidential adviser discussion and June 22 follow-up on Deny Flight, radar information, SEAD, RRF support and sanctions.

chronology.label: bosnia svits 11/17
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. Jones relays discussion of Bihac, Rose/Clark views, exclusion zones and alliance friction, plus public guidance about U.S. activities.

chronology.label: bosnia svits 10/14
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. October 14 notes describe tentative policy agreement awaiting Principals review, drafting an arms-lift resolution and reviewing military options.

chronology.label: bosnia svits 9/30
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. September 30 notes examine possible Nunn funding constraints on embargo enforcement and concerns about premature claims that the border was closed.

chronology.label: bosnia svits 9/27
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. September 27 notes discuss a possible ministerial Contact Group meeting, delayed embargo lift and staffing sanctions monitors.

chronology.label: List  of  Invitees to War  Crimes  Tribunal  Discussion April  30,  1993,  Washington,  DC
chronology.note: Catalog document date retained; undated documents are not assigned a date from neighboring files. List identifies invitees for an April 30, 1993 war crimes tribunal discussion and says invitations were sent April 13.
